question: Can a tuned TF-IDF (word+char n-gram) model with context-candidate overlap features and class-imbalance handling beat a Naive Bayes n-gram baseline at recognizing genuine cited legal principles (holdings)?
method: CaseHOLD (LexGLUE) proxy: each context has 1 true holding and 4 distractors, each candidate a binary instance. Train contexts subsampled from the train split, held-out contexts subsampled from the official test split. Hyperparameters and decision threshold chosen by context-grouped 3-fold CV on train only; test used once.
baseline: Multinomial Naive Bayes on word 1-2gram counts of the candidate (alpha tuned by CV).
improved: Logistic regression on word+char TF-IDF of the candidate plus context-candidate overlap features (raw and centred within context), CV-tuned C and class weighting.
notes: Proxy dataset (US case law, not UK BAILII) so results are not comparable to the paper. Both models use an F1-optimal threshold picked from out-of-fold train scores. TF-IDF vocabularies are fit unsupervised on train candidates before CV. Best params: baseline {'multinomialnb__alpha': 0.5}, improved {'C': 0.3, 'class_weight': None}. Single run, single seed, no confidence intervals; the test set is subsampled.
